title: AI-ranked SARS-CoV-2 protein interactions guide discovery of an NSP10–NSP16 inhibitor
summary: A machine-learning classifier applied to quantitative PPI assay data and AlphaFold-Multimer predictions to prioritize SARS-CoV-2 protein interactions; 15 of 34 high-confidence interactions were not previously listed in IMEx. The team then targeted the NSP10–NSP16 methyltransferase interface in an ultra-large virtual screen. Compound 459 bound NSP10 (MST affinity about 13 μM), reduced NSP10–NSP16 interaction in cells (BRET IC50 9.2 μM), inhibited complex methyltransferase activity by about 50% at 100 μM, and reduced SARS-CoV-2 reporter replication in cells (IC50 39.5 μM).
ai_technology: Multi-adaptive support-vector-machine (maSVM) classifier for quantitative protein–protein interaction data, coupled with AlphaFold-Multimer complex prediction; VirtualFlow/QuickVina2 and later docking methods performed compound screening
organization: Max Delbrück Center for Molecular Medicine; University of Luxembourg; University of California, San Francisco; Harvard Medical School; University of California, San Diego; University of Toronto; University of Cambridge; University of Antwerp and collaborators

evidence.tested: A machine-learning classifier applied to quantitative PPI assay data and AlphaFold-Multimer predictions to prioritize SARS-CoV-2 protein interactions; 15 of 34 high-confidence interactions were not previously listed in IMEx.
evidence.unknown: The paper reports an experimental small-molecule hit, not a drug or clinical effect. Compound 459 has micromolar affinity and cellular antiviral IC50; authors explicitly state it requires extensive optimization. Methyltransferase inhibition was about 50% at 100 μM in one initial assay; subsequent data include cellular interaction and reporter-replication experiments. The NSP10–NSP16 interface was previously known and had prior virtual screening, but this paper reports a different compound scaffold and tested outcomes; shared target does not make this a duplicate. In vitro and cell assays do not demonstrate efficacy in animals or people.
evidence.ai_role: The maSVM algorithm prioritized PPI interactions using quantitative LuTHy binary-assay data and AlphaFold-Multimer predictions, supporting selection and mapping of SARS-CoV-2 interactions, including the NSP10–NSP16 interface and interface hot spots. The drug-like compound hit itself was identified by VirtualFlow and docking against the selected interface, not generated by the classifier. Compound 459 was then experimentally tested for protein binding, interaction disruption, methyltransferase activity and viral replication.
